To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the total sum of squared errors, the residual sum squared errors, the sum of squared errors due to the regression, the total sum of cross products, the residual sum cross products, the sum of cross products due to the regression and the total sum of products of squared errors, can all be written in terms of the reproducing kernels of the Hilbert spaces associated with the functional data.
the total sum of square, the residual sum squares, and the sums of squares due to regressions are all quadratic forms of Hilbert-valued random variables.

the total sum of the squares is the norm squared of the projection of the response vector on the linear subspace spanned by the regression functions; the residual sum of the squares equals the norm squared of a projection error; and the sum of the squares due to the linear regression equals the norm squared difference between the norm squared of this projection and the norm squared of its projection error.
